Article Title: MLC election results: Congress faces setback across 4 states; state-wise results and key wins
Article Text:
The biennial elections for these Graduate and Teacher constituencies across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, and Maharashtra were held via ballot papers on October 23, 2026, with counting beginning on October 27, 2026.

Here is a state-wise look at the latest results and counting trends.

Karnataka (4 seats): BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four, Congress draws blank

Uttar Pradesh (11 seats): BJP wins four seats, SP secures two

Bihar (8 seats): Jan Suraaj opens account, RJD defeats BJP veteran

Maharashtra (5 seats): BJP's Sudhakar Kohale leads Congress in Nagpur

NEW DELHI: Congress faced a major setback in the legislative council elections on Wednesday, failing to secure a victory in the seats declared so far across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Maharashtra, even as counting continued in several constituencies.The BJP -JD(S) alliance swept all four seats in Karnataka, where the ruling Congress drew a blank despite having a majority in the state Assembly. The BJP retained three constituencies, while the JD(S) wrested the Bengaluru Teachers’ seat from the Congress.In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP and Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins, while in Bihar, Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party opened its legislative council account by defeating the Congress. The RJD also scored a victory in Bihar, wresting the Patna Teachers’ seat from the BJP.Counting for 28 legislative council seats across Uttar Pradesh (11), Bihar (8), Maharashtra (5) and Karnataka (4) began on Tuesday following polling on October 23. The elections were held for graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies, with results declared for several seats and counting continuing in others.The BJP-JD(S) alliance swept all four legislative council seats in Karnataka, dealing a setback to the ruling Congress.The BJP retained the North-East Teachers’, South-East Graduates’ and West Graduates’ constituencies, while its ally JD(S) wrested the Bengaluru Teachers’ seat from the Congress.JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated sitting Congress MLC Puttanna by 908 votes in Bengaluru Teachers’. Ranganath secured 10,810 votes against Puttanna’s 9,902.BJP’s Shashil G Namoshi retained North-East Teachers’ by 3,297 votes, securing his fifth victory from the constituency with 15,596 votes against Congress candidate Sharanappa Mattur’s 12,299.In South-East Graduates’, BJP candidate K M Suresh defeated Congress nominee Shashi Hulikunte Mutt by 23,098 votes. Sitting BJP MLC S V Sankanur retained West Graduates’, defeating Congress candidate Mohan Limbikai by 9,323 votes.The results marked a clean sweep for the opposition alliance, with the Congress failing to win a single seat despite campaigning by chief minister D K Shivakumar, former chief minister Siddaramaiah and other senior leaders.However, the results are not expected to affect the stability of the Congress government or significantly alter the balance of power in the 75-member Legislative Council.The BJP won four of the 11 Uttar Pradesh legislative council seats, while the SP secured two, according to the latest confirmed results.The BJP retained the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ seat, where Hari Singh Dhillon defeated SP’s Danish Akhtar by 17,676 votes. It also won the Lucknow Teachers’ seat, with Umesh Dwivedi defeating SP candidate Sushil Kumar by 6,992 votes. The party also won both the Meerut Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituencies.The SP won the Varanasi Teachers’ seat through Lal Bihari Yadav and the Agra-Aligarh Teachers’ seat, where Akash Agrawal defeated BJP nominee Hari Kishore Tiwari.In the Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates’ constituency, SP candidate Mansingh Yadav secured 27,157 votes after the fifth round, against BJP candidate Ashok Rathore’s 7,648. SP candidates were also leading in the Varanasi and Lucknow Graduates’ constituencies.BJP candidate Manvendra Singh was leading in the Agra-Aligarh Graduates’ constituency.In the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ seat, BJP candidate Dhruv Kumar Tripathi received 11,881 votes against independent candidate Rajiv Yadav’s 11,415 after the final round, though disputes arose over the counting process. The SP alleged irregularities and boycotted the counting process.Meanwhile, an additional commissioner was removed following a candidate’s complaint after 52 more votes were found in a ballot box from Mau than recorded in the official data.The Bihar legislative council elections delivered several upsets, with the BJP, RJD, Jan Suraaj Party and an Independent winning one Teachers’ constituency each.Jan Suraaj Party candidate Suresh Prasad Rai defeated sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha by 324 votes in the Darbhanga Teachers’ constituency, officials said on Wednesday. The victory marked the party’s first win in the Bihar Legislative Council.BJP candidate Narendra Prasad Singh won the Tirhut Teachers’ seat, defeating independent candidate Bhushan Kumar Jha.In another major result, RJD candidate Dr Sanjeev Kumar defeated the BJP’s veteran MLC Nawal Kishore Yadav in the Patna Teachers’ constituency, ending his long hold on the seat.Independent candidate Rahul Raj also defeated sitting MLC Afaq Ahmed in the Saran Teachers’ constituency.Meanwhile, JD(U)’s Neeraj Kumar was leading RJD candidate Dilip Rai in Patna Graduates’, with reports indicating a victory for the JD(U) leader, although the official result was awaited in the latest update.Counting continued in the remaining Graduates’ constituencies.The polls will decide the fate of 90 candidates in four graduates’ constituencies and 60 candidates in four teachers’ constituencies. Turnout stood at 82.85% in teachers’ constituencies and 53.42% in graduates’ seats.Counting continued for five Maharashtra legislative council seats, with BJP candidate Sudhakar Kohale leading sitting Congress MLC Abhijit Wanjari by 4,294 votes in the Nagpur Division Graduates’ constituency after the second round.Kohale secured 60,924 votes against Wanjari’s 56,630, while independent candidate Nitesh Karale received 24,249 votes. A total of 15,106 votes were declared invalid.None of the candidates had reached the winning quota of 75,438 votes, with the final outcome dependent on further counting and the transfer of preferential votes.In the Amravati Teachers’ constituency, Shiv Sena candidate Kiran Sarnaik was also leading as counting continued.The polls, held on October 23, saw 182 candidates contesting across three graduates’ and two teachers’ constituencies. The results are being watched amid rebel candidates, alliance differences and efforts by the BJP-led Mahayuti and the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi to consolidate support.The terms of the sitting members are due to end on December 6, and the election process is scheduled to be completed by October 31.
Article Summary: BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four legislative council seats in Karnataka. RJD also scored a victory in Bihar, wresting the Patna Teachers’ seat from the BJP. Results are not expected to affect the stability of the Congress government.

Article Title: Cabinet secretary lists 12 types of secretaries: File throwers, file sitters, latecomers...
Article Text:
Cabinet secretary T V Somanathan presented a humorous but pointed classification of 12 types of secretaries at a performance review meeting

Clustered near-10 scores make it tough to pick out stars: CabSec

NEW DELHI: It began as a regular meeting. But the senior bureaucrats who had gathered at a performance review meeting on Tuesday were in for a surprise — and not a particularly pleasant one, even though the point was made with a generous dose of humour.Cabinet secretary T V Somanathan unveiled a presentation on 12 types of bureaucrats, which is believed to have left many present at the meeting squirming. Among the types listed by Somanathan were officers who ask women colleagues to come a bit too close for comfort to show them a document; those who throw files and speak rudely; and those who call in staff on Saturdays, then arrive late themselves.Other entries included officers who call meetings after 7pm, sit on files, or send ministers decisions they could take themselves. Each type was accompanied by a cartoon, in many cases work by TOI’s legendary cartoonist R K Laxman.Apart from cartoons and indirect criticism, there was a quantitative component to the meeting too — the secretaries of various govt departments were ranked on various performance parameters.The CabSec’s broader message, officials said, was about running better meetings and making the workplace more conducive to getting things done.He also informed officers about the Centre’s plans to roll out the next round of reforms, Deregulation 3.0, from Jan, aiming to cut red tape, simplify compliance and improve the ease of doing business.At a meeting of senior bureaucrats on Tuesday, Union cabinet secretary T V Somanathan urged faster inter-ministerial consultations. Union finance and commerce ministries, Somanathan is learnt to have said, should send their views promptly to avoid any delays. The cabinet secretary also noted that officers’ performance scores often cluster close to 10 on a scale of 1 to 10, leaving the ranking system with little room to demarcate the stars from the merely satisfactory.Meanwhile, the department of food and public distribution took the opportunity to flag that around 1 lakh railway employees have ration cards allowing them to receive free foodgrain under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana.Calling it a disciplinary issue, Somanathan directed Railway Board chairman Satish Kumar to ensure that the employees surrender their ration cards.Last month, the food department had written to the cabinet secretary about ration cards being used to establish family identity under Ayushman Bharat’s Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY) scheme, even though they are not a formal eligibility requirement.
Article Summary: Cabinet secretary T V Somanathan unveiled a presentation on 12 types of bureaucrats. Each type was accompanied by a cartoon, in many cases work by TOI’s legendary cartoonist R K Laxman. The cabinet secretary also noted that officers’ performance scores often cluster close to 10, leaving the ranking system with little room to demarcate the stars.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi, whose memoir will be released in November, said on Tuesday that there would be “tamasha” after the book’s release.According to the former Congress president, the book gave her an opportunity to tell her story because many things written about her are either “exaggerated” or completely “invented. ”“I felt that since a lot had been written about me, and a lot of it was not quite correct, or you know, it was either invented or exaggerated, so it gave me a feel of being able to now put down my story and describe facts and things as they were, as they really were,” Sonia Gandhi said in a video on X, which she joined recently.The Congress parliamentary party chief further stated that reading her memoir may change some people’s views about her, while others may develop a more negative opinion.“People have different views. Some people may change their view about me. Some people’s view may become worse, but that’s what it is. That’s what happens when you write a book or when you are in public life. There’s bound to be tamasha, as you would say it here,” she added.The memoir, titled "Belonging: A Journey of Love," traces Sonia Gandhi's journey from her childhood in post-war Italy to her relationship with former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and the personal losses that shaped her life and relationship with India.The memoir will be published internationally by Alfred A Knopf, an imprint of the Knopf Doubleday Publishing Group, on November 10. The announcement was made on August 18.However, the book’s release in India faced uncertainty after a disagreement between Penguin Random House India and Sonia Gandhi’s representatives over editorial changes that her team refused to accept.HarperCollins India later stepped in to publish the Indian edition, which is expected to be released on November 10, the same day as the international edition.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love," will be released in November. The book traces Sonia Gandhi's journey from her childhood in post-war Italy to her relationship with former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. The memoir will be published internationally by Alfred A Knopf on November 10.

Article Title: Is Jagan Reddy's 'regret' message a calculated alliance pitch for Congress?
Article Text:
A successful alliance with the INDIA bloc hinges on the YSRCP and Congress aligning, which could be Jagan Mohan Reddy’s biggest challenge

Jagan’s support for NDA’s key Bills

Jagan vs Congress

The 2029 challenge

NEW DELHI: Is YSRCP supremo YS Jagan Mohan Reddy signalling a drift towards the Congress-led INDIA bloc? Or is he trying to break free from the image of being soft on the BJP The former Andhra Pradesh chief minister has provided issue-based support to the BJP-led NDA government on several key legislations in Parliament while he was in power in the state. However, he has stayed away from joining any alliance till now. So, when Jagan Reddy recently regretted his “mistake” of supporting the 2023 NDA legislation for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner, it fuelled speculation about his future political moves."We regret supporting the process under which the ruling party nominates the Chief Election Commissioner at the Centre. Neither the CEC nor the SEC should be appointed by the ruling party. The selection committee should comprise the Prime Minister, the leader of the opposition and the Chief Justice of India (CJI), with all three exercising their voting rights," the YSRCP chief said recently, calling the current selection system "flawed. "The timing and context of Jagan’s remarks are significant. So, is he rethinking his “solo” politics? And if yes, will the Congress be ready to tango with him in Andhra Pradesh? After all, alliances with regional parties have been the Congress’s biggest Achilles heel across states.Jagan Mohan Reddy’s MPs backed the Modi government several times between 2019 and 2024, both in Lok Sabha and in Rajya Sabha, on many important legislations. However, when it came to stitching an alliance for the 2024 elections, the BJP ignored Jagan’s help and joined hands with his arch-rival Chandrababu Naidu. Together, TDP and BJP swept the polls in Andhra Pradesh, winning 164 out of 175 seats in the assembly and 21 out of 25 seats in Lok Sabha. The YSRCP was reduced to 11 seats in the assembly and 4 in Lok Sabha.Despite being spurned by the BJP and his party’s shock defeat, Jagan Mohan Reddy remained confident about his BJP ties. After all, he still had 15 MPs (4 in Lok Sabha and 11 in Rajya Sabha) to provide the much-needed support to the BJP’s minority government at the Centre. Jagan even announced that his MPs would extend issue-based support to the NDA government in matters concerning national and state interest.But with the BJP heavily dependent on Chandrababu Naidu’s support for survival of its government at the Centre, there was little room for the saffron party to accommodate Jagan Reddy. Nearly two and a half years down the line, Reddy seems to have accepted this harsh reality and is perhaps gearing up to chart a new path for the next political challenge in 2029.However, for any successful alliance with the INDIA bloc - the YSRCP and the Congress will have to be on the same page. And that perhaps would be the biggest challenge for Jagan Mohan Reddy.Jagan Mohan Reddy had a bitter parting from the Congress in 2010, a year after the death of his father YS Rajasekhara Reddy. YSR Reddy was in his second term as the chief minister of Andhra Pradesh when he died in a helicopter crash on September 2, 2009. Jagan’s supporters, who were many in number, lobbied hard with the Congress high command for the top post, but Sonia Gandhi did not budge and made K Rosaiah the chief minister. The Congress leadership did not approve of Jagan’s Odarpu Yatra, which was part of his announced plan to meet the families of many people who had sacrificed their lives after his father’s death.That set the stage for his eventual exit from the Congress, which he announced on November 29, 2010 in an open letter to Sonia Gandhi carefully written to ensure there was enough public sympathy for his second phase of political career.In the 2014 assembly elections, the YSRCP made an impressive debut and won 67 out of the 175 seats with a vote share of 44.46%, while the Congress could manage only a vote share of 2.8%. The Congress decision to bifurcate the state and create Telangana played a huge role in the party’s declining political fortunes in the state.On November 6, 2017, Jagan embarked on the Praja Sankalpa Yatra and covered 3,648 km in 341 days, crossing 134 assembly constituencies. The Yatra, from YSR Ghat at Idupulapaya to the northeastern tip of Ichchapuram, powered Jagan Mohan Reddy to a historic mandate of 151 seats in the 175-member assembly in the 2019 elections. The Congress’s vote share was reduced to less than 1%.The Congress, since then, has been making efforts to reclaim its lost political space in the state. It roped in Jagan Reddy’s sister Y S Sharmila as part of the party’s revival plan. Sharmila, who started her political career with her brother Jagan Mohan Reddy eventually drifted towards the Congress and was appointed president of Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee in January 2024.However, both Jagan Mohan Reddy and his sister Y S Sharmila failed to make an impact in the 2024 elections. The 2024 elections saw a dramatic collapse of Jagan’s electoral fortunes, and his party was reduced to only 11 seats. The Congress once again failed to make its presence felt.And that brings us to the 2029 elections - a do-or-die challenge for both Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress. Jagan’s remark on backing the CEC appointment Bill is his first open “regret” for backing the BJP.But does this “open regret” mean an olive branch for the Congress?Former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha strongly feels that Jagan and Congress should come together, though he admits that this may not be easy.“Politics is the art of the possible and I'm sure Jaganmohan Reddy is aware that Chandrababu Naidu has been an extremely close alliance partner of the Modi government. While the Congress doesn't have a base in Andhra like it used to have once upon a time. The support base of Jaganmohan Reddy is basically the Congress vote which moved away from the traditional Congress to the Congress that Jaganmohan Reddy, branded as the Congress of his father. So, if the merger were to happen, it would, frankly speaking, give them a huge advantage because then both the Central Congress and the Jaganmohan Congress could be on the same page,” Sanjay Jha says.However, he accepts that merger of the two parties could be a difficult process while stitching an alliance may be easier. “Once a political party becomes independent and has power, they don't like to give it up in a hurry. The TMC or the NCP are good examples. In which case it could be an alliance,” Sanjay Jha adds.The third option, according to Sanjay Jha, is for the Congress to resurrect itself on its own strongly in Andhra by capturing both the anti-incumbent votes against Chandrababu Naidu and winning back the loyalist voters of the Congress who had moved over to Jaganmohan Reddy.This is easier said than done. The Congress has a poor track record when it comes to winning back states it has lost. We have seen several states across the country where the Congress has lost its government and eventually its support base but does little to reclaim it.In Andhra Pradesh, Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP are going all out to consolidate their position. Naidu’s call for greater cooperation and coordination among southern states at a recent conference is perhaps an effort to keep his importance and relevance intact. We saw DMK’s MK Stalin make similar moves before he lost power to Vijay’s TVK in the last assembly elections.Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress face an uphill electoral battle in 2029. It will be interesting to see if they can agree to an alliance to take on Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP.
Article Summary: Jagan Mohan Reddy had a bitter parting from the Congress in 2010, a year after the death of his father YS Rajasekhara Reddy. The former Andhra Pradesh chief minister has provided issue-based support to the BJP-led NDA government on several key legislations in Parliament. For any successful alliance with the INDIA bloc - the YSRCP and the Congress will have to be on the same page.

Article Title: ‘BJP wins through foul means’: Akhilesh alleges MLC poll fraud, warns of 2027 defeat
Article Text:
Akhilesh alleges conspiracy to defeat SP candidate in UP MLC polls, targets BJP

SP candidates allege irregularities in MLC counting

SP claims lead in Lucknow constituency

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party supremo Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party of electoral malpractice in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC) elections, alleging that irregularities during counting were part of a conspiracy to defeat SP candidate Sanjayan Tripathi.In a post on X, Akhilesh alleged that BJP leaders, their associates and officials had colluded to manipulate the counting process. He claimed that the alleged treatment of Tripathi had angered teachers and members of his community, and vowed that the SP would fight "injustice and harassment.""The corrupt BJP leaders, their conspiratorial associates and complicit officials have stooped to every possible low to win the MLC elections. The conspiracy to defeat Dr Sanjayan Tripathi has been exposed before everyone. The reason for defeating Dr Sanjayan Tripathi through vote-counting irregularities is not merely that he is an SP candidate; the main reason behind it is “Haata nahi bhaata” (he is not acceptable to them). In matters of politics, the BJP has sunk to the lowest depths. After such massive fraud, the public has realised that the BJP has, in fact, lost every seat," he wrote."BJP leaders win not through votes, but through foul means," former UP CM added.Targeting the BJP over its alleged treatment of teachers, the SP chief said the incident had left a deep impression on Tripathi's community and teachers across the state.“The way Sanjayan Tripathi has been harassed is being witnessed by his entire community. Neither his community nor any teacher in the state will forget Dr. Tripathi's tears,” the SP chief said, alleging that teachers had received nothing but humiliation from the BJP government.Akhilesh also linked the controversy to the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, claiming that teachers would remember the alleged mistreatment when they vote.“Every teacher will always remember the despicable conspiracy to make teachers do the unwanted task of collecting fodder, and will fulfil their “guru resolve” by defeating the BJP in the 2027 assembly elections,” he wrote.Taking another swipe at the ruling party, Akhilesh said its alleged electoral tactics would not succeed across the state."The BJP's “400 BC” (a pun on char sau beesi, meaning fraud or deceit) will not work across all 403 seats," he further said.Reiterating his support for Tripathi, the SP chief added, "We stand with Sanjayan Tripathi and against every injustice and act of harassment inflicted upon him and his community. We stand united against the BJP and will continue to do so."The remarks came amid allegations of irregularities during the counting of votes for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Division Teachers' constituency. SP candidate Sanjayan Tripathi and independent candidate Rajeev Yadav boycotted the counting process, accusing administrative officials and the election observer of favouring the BJP candidate.Speaking to news agency ANI, Tripathi alleged that the counting trend changed abruptly after the first three rounds, when independent candidate Rajeev Yadav was leading by around 450 votes.“We have boycotted the vote-counting process. Everything was proceeding smoothly for the first three rounds of counting; independent candidate Rajiv Yadav was leading by approximately 450 votes. Suddenly, the counting began to shift entirely in favour of the BJP candidate; the trend changed abruptly, making it appear as though the outcome had been predetermined. Consequently, we decided to boycott the process,” Tripathi said.He also alleged police misconduct and claimed that the authorities were determined to ensure the ruling party's candidate won.A day earlier, Akhilesh had urged Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to take immediate cognisance of the alleged irregularities and ensure transparency in the counting process. He had accused officials of delaying the announcement of round-wise results and warned that the SP would launch a movement and file a case against the Election Commission if any foul play was detected.Similar allegations were raised by SP candidate Danish Akhtar over the results in the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers' constituency. Akhtar alleged irregularities in the electoral rolls and voting process, claiming that 30 per cent of the names on the electoral roll were fraudulent. He also accused the Election Commission of failing to act despite receiving evidence and repeated representations.Meanwhile, in Lucknow, Ram Singh Rana, an SP agent for party candidate Kanti Singh, claimed on Wednesday that the party was maintaining its lead during counting. He alleged that BJP candidate Avnish Singh had repeatedly attempted to disrupt the process.“We have been steadily increasing our lead since yesterday, and it continues to grow. The opposition candidate from the BJP made several attempts to misuse power, but the Samajwadi youth did not bow down; they stood firm and remained unafraid--even when there were lathi-charges during the night, and chairs were smashed,” Rana said.Rana alleged that the opposition had tried to halt the counting process four or five times and that SP workers had faced harassment throughout the night."The opposition tried to halt the process four or five times, but no one gave in or felt intimidated. We have maintained our momentum and are moving toward victory. We faced harassment all night long. The opposition candidate, Avnish Singh, tried to stop the process five times, but we did not back down," Rana said.Sharing the vote figures after four rounds of counting, Rana said Kanti Singh had secured 25,382 votes, while the BJP candidate had received 17,797 votes.“As the counting for the fifth round begins, the margin is significant, and we are continuing to pull further ahead,” he added.Polling for five Graduates' constituencies and six Teachers' constituencies in Uttar Pradesh concluded on October 23, with counting held on October 27.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party supremo Akhilesh Yadav accuses Bharatiya Janata Party of electoral malpractice. Alleges irregularities during counting were part of a conspiracy to defeat SP candidate Sanjayan Tripathi. Targeting the BJP over its alleged treatment of teachers, the SP chief said the incident had left a deep impression on Tripathi's community.

NEW DELHI: BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal are in an advanced stage of negotiations for reviving their alliance for the Punjab assembly elections A couple of thorny issues, including the precise seat-sharing arrangement and the accommodation of the rebel Akali faction, seen close to BJP, continue to persist but several functionaries from the two parties believe they can be addressed in the coming days.Before Sukhbir Singh Badal-led Akali Dal snapped ties with BJP due to its opposition to now-repealed farm laws in 2020 as a section of farmers launched protest against the reforms, his party was the decidedly big brother in Punjab. Its decline since, brought afore by the 2022 assembly and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, and BJP's gains since mean that their equation is likely to be rearranged.Sources said BJP's share can nearly double from the 23 assembly seats it used to contest in the 117-member House as an ally of SAD.With talks still going on and BJP keen to offer a respectable deal to splinter Akali group (Punar Surjit), the seat-sharing deal remains a work in progress.BJP on its part has maintained it is preparing to contest on all seats after bagging over 18% votes, its best ever, in 2024 when two main rivals for office- governing AAP and the main opposition Congress- pulling around 26% votes. SAD's share fell to a little over 13%.What has boosted the prospect of an alliance is the view that this can be their best shot at power and energise the social compact of Hindu-Sikh harmony, which was an early inspiration for their alliance in the 90s, in the sensitive border state where a newbie party Waris Punjab De of jailed MP Amritpal Singh is peddling a more extreme agenda.Home minister Amit Shah's recent assertion that NDA will win the next Punjab assembly polls and Badal's expression of openness to joining hands with parties other AAP and Congress have turned back the focus on the possibility of their alliance.
Article Summary: BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal are in an advanced stage of negotiations for reviving their alliance for the Punjab assembly elections. A couple of thorny issues, including the precise seat-sharing arrangement and the accommodation of the rebel Akali faction, seen close to BJP, continue to persist.

The Bombay High Court extended actor Imran Khan's deadline to leave India until November 2 and scheduled a hearing on his challenge to an FRRO notice directing him to leave the country. Khan, who holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, has argued that the notice violates his constitutional rights and was issued without giving him an opportunity to respond. The notice followed an FIR linked to an alleged protest in Mumbai on October 10 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Karnataka's final electoral roll recorded 4,54,55,689 voters after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), down from the original electorate of around 5.5 crore. Of the voters removed during the exercise, 65.45 lakh were classified as permanently shifted. The final list includes 6.83 lakh new voters, while 61,867 people were excluded following the notices phase. The state has around four lakh more female voters than male voters.Union minister Kiren Rijiju demanded an apology from the Congress after the Indian Army debunked an AI-generated video falsely attributing remarks about Chinese control of areas in Arunachal Pradesh to Lieutenant General Girish Kalia.The Army said the video had been digitally altered and that the original footage was from a 2023 press briefing in Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir, concerning infiltration attempts along the Line of Control. It clarified that the officer had made no remarks about Chinese control of Arunachal Pradesh or the denial of supplies to Indian troops.Israelis voted in a crucial parliamentary election as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced a challenge from rival political blocs seeking to unseat him. Reports of missing, damaged and defaced ballot slips prompted the Yashar party, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, to file a complaint with the Central Elections Committee. Turnout reached 31.5% by noon, the highest recorded at that hour since 1973, according to The Times of Israel. Arab-led parties could play a decisive role in government formation if neither major political bloc secures a majority.Abhishek Sharma and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set a world record for the highest scoring rate in a 100-plus opening partnership in men's T20 internationals, scoring at 18.13 runs per over against New Zealand in Wellington. Abhishek smashed 113 off 38 balls, while Sooryavanshi contributed 45 off 18 deliveries as the pair added 133 runs in seven overs. Their explosive start helped India chase down 199 in 13.2 overs, securing a six-wicket victory and completing a 3-0 series sweep.
Article Summary: Karnataka's final electoral roll recorded 4.54 crore voters after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), marking a reduction of nearly one crore from the original electorate. Article Title: 'Won't rest till puppet Gyanesh is removed': Cong claims denied permit for mock CEC impeachment; Delhi Police clarifies

Delhi Police's 'terms and conditions'

NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday accused the Centre of denying permission for an event where INDIA bloc parties planned a "public impeachment" of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, ahead of their November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan.Congress general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal said the government-run Ashoka Hotel had initially allowed the event to be held on its premises but later denied permission following police intervention."The day before yesterday, our people came to construct the infrastructure here and the police stopped them. We don't know what the reason is," Venugopal said."This means it is not the Delhi Police's decision. It is the decision of PM Modi and Amit Shah, and they are protecting their puppet Gyanesh Kumar," he alleged.In a social media post on X, Venugopal also accused the Delhi Police of stopping the party doing the set up for the event at Ramlila Maidan."How many permissions will you deny, Mr. Amit Shah? How many people will you stop? 21 parties of the INDIA bloc had planned a Public Impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar as a curtain raiser to the Nov 1st Mega Rally and March - first at Hotel Ashoka, where permission was denied, and then at Ramleela Maidan, where despite already having all the requisite permissions, Delhi Police stopped us from doing the set up for the event.First they destroy the electoral system, and now they are trying all kinds of tricks to silence those who fight to save our democracy," Venugopal said."Let it be very clear, come what may, we will not rest until Modi-Shah's puppet Gyanesh Kumar is not removed. If they stop us here, we will go to Amit Shah's house, PM Modi's house, and stage a massive dharna there. But we will fight to the finish, and until our mission is accomplished," he added.The proposed event is part of a series of protests by the Congress and other opposition parties demanding Kumar's resignation over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged electoral irregularities.Meanwhile, Delhi Police said it had not withdrawn permission for the Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan, adding that there had been no change in the earlier approval.On the proposed mock Parliament event at Ashoka Hotel, police sources said the matter rested with the hotel, as the premises were privately owned."With respect to the Ashoka Hotel mock Parliament, Delhi Police says it depends on the hotel since it's their private premises," Delhi Police sources told news agency ANI.Earlier, Delhi Police had confirmed that a no-objection certificate (NOC) had been issued to the Congress for booking Ramlila Maidan from October 25 to November 3. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said the Congress had approached the police after obtaining a venue availability certificate from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD).Delhi Police has also laid down a list of "terms and conditions" for the Congress rally on November 1, including installing high-definition CCTV cameras at strategic locations, ensuring the event concludes by 5pm and prohibiting speeches that could disturb communal harmony.In its communication to the Congress, police said there was "no objection" to the rally from a law-and-order perspective, subject to prior permission from the land-owning authority and compliance with the stipulated conditions.The organisers have been asked to install cameras at "all the strategic points including entry/exit gates, stage, all surrounding areas of Ram Lila Ground and sitting enclosures", along with a monitoring system with "atleast 5 screens" and a CCTV control room.They have also been directed to provide "sufficient numbers of water tankers and toilet blocks (separate for female participants)" and deploy volunteers wearing "identical dress or bear common Badges" to ensure the smooth conduct of the rally.The rally must conclude at 5pm on November 1, after which "the dispersal will start and under no circumstance will it be extended". Overnight stays by participants at Ramlila Maidan, either before or after the rally, have also been prohibited.Police has further directed the organisers to ensure that "no speakers would speak anything about caste/creed/colour that can disturb the public harmony, peace and tranquility of the area".If any "instigating/intimidating speech" is made, "the PA system will be switched off immediately", followed by the removal of the speaker from the stage by the organisers.
Article Summary: Congress accuses Centre of denying permission for event where INDIA bloc parties planned a "public impeachment" of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Article Title: 'Not in line with expectations': UP CEO apologises for 'thank God Ram didn't hit any minority' post
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh CEO Navdeep Rinwa on Tuesday issued an apology for his office's sarcastic reply to Aam Aadmi Party MP Sanjay Singh over allegations of caste bias following an erroneous voter slip entry, saying that the language and tone of the post were not in line with the nature of communication expected from the poll body.The UP CEO said the outrage generated by the social media post had been duly noted and that future communication would be polite and formal."The language, tone, and sharp nature of the comments in the quoted post of this handle are not in line with the nature of communication expected from this official handle. The genuine outrage generated by the comments in the post has been duly noted," the UP CEO said in a post on X."We sincerely apologise to those who are surprised and upset by this. From now on, our communication will be polite and formal," it added.This comes a day after Sanjay Singh questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over an erroneous entry in a voter slip in which "Ramhit Yadav" became "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara".In a post on X in Hindi, Singh said, "Gyanesh Kumar ji, why did Ram hit only a Yadav? Why did Ram not hit any Singh, Pathak, Asthana, Sharma, Rai or Bisht? Is your computer casteist? Are you running the agenda of any political party?"In a sarcastic reply to Singh, the UP CEO's official X handle said that had the entry read that Ram hit a minority, the authorities would have been accused of communalism too."A strange name, 'Ram ne Sharma ko Maara', is also present in the voter list of the recent legislative council elections. Computers/software are not casteist," the UP CEO said."We accept that an error was made, but fortunately, even while making the error, no caste discrimination took place. Thank God that Ram did not hit a minority. Otherwise, besides being accused of casteism, we would have also faced allegations of communalism," it added.The CEO's office also shared a voter slip from the recently held graduate constituency legislative council elections. The slip listed the voter's name as Ravi Sharma, while his father's name appeared as "Ram ne Sharma ko Maara".The exchange comes days after instances of erroneous entries in electoral records were flagged, raising questions over the computer software used to prepare voter lists.Later, UP CEO Navdeep Rinwa, in a post on X, said some "bizarre-looking names" had appeared in the voter list during the recently held legislative council elections."The reasons behind such mistakes are being looked into and appropriate action is being taken to prevent recurrence," the CEO said.He said "some forged voter slips" had gone viral on social media and were being displayed or circulated by several established media outlets and prominent individuals. "The person responsible for the forgery will be dealt with as per law," Rinwa added.Last week, Rinwa had explained that the software was designed to transliterate names entered in English into Hindi.However, in some cases, instead of transliterating names, it translated the words, resulting in incorrect entries. For instance, if "Ramhit Yadav" was mistakenly typed as "Ram Hit Yadav", the software translated it into Hindi as "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara" (Ram hit Yadav). He said the errors could have been corrected using the editing feature, but some remained in the final list.Another instance, in which "B.Com" was entered in place of the father's name in the electoral roll for the legislative council polls, appeared to be a case of human error or negligence, the CEO had said.
Article Summary: UP CEO Navdeep Rinwa apologises for sarcastic reply to Aam Aadmi Party MP Sanjay Singh over allegations of caste bias. Singh questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over an erroneous entry in a voter slip in which "Ramhit Yadav" became "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara" Rinwa said future communication would be polite and formal.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter addressed the situation during an appearance onon Monday, confirming that the Chiefs have contacted teams about potential wide receiver additions.“You know, they have been calling around, and I don’t think it would be a surprise to see them continue to attempt to add a wide receiver before the trade deadline, two weeks from tomorrow,” Schefter said. “Whether they can get it done, we’ll see.”His comments suggest that the Chiefs are actively searching for reinforcements, even as uncertainty surrounds the available trade targets.The injuries to Rice and Thornton have weakened Kansas City's options at receiver.That leaves the team looking for someone who can make an immediate impact as the season progresses.Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas has emerged as a possible target. Hill suffered a dislocated left knee and multiple ligament tears during the 2024 season. Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “I didn’t want my children to be like me.” - How Mike Tyson turned the heartbreak of losing daughter into a father’s redemption and enduring legacy
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “I didn’t want my children to be like me.” - How Mike Tyson turned the heartbreak of losing daughter into a father’s redemption and enduring legacy

How did Mike Tyson’s childhood in Brownsville shape him

How did the death of Exodus Tyson change Mike Tyson

Why did Mike Tyson want his children to have different lives?

How are Amir Tyson and Miguel Tyson building their own paths

What makes Mike Tyson’s story as a father meaningful

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mike Tyson’s life has been shaped by boxing victories, personal struggles and the loss of his four-year-old daughter, Exodus, in 2009. The former heavyweight champion has also spoken openly about how fatherhood changed his outlook on life. Although the world remembers Tyson for his power inside the ring, his experiences as a parent offer another side of his story. From growing up in Brooklyn to raising seven children, his journey shows how a difficult past can shape a person’s hopes for the next generation.Mike Tyson grew up in Brownsville, Brooklyn, where he faced bullying and trouble at a young age. His father was largely absent from his life, and his childhood brought experiences that later influenced his behaviour and his boxing career.Tyson found direction through boxing after meeting trainer Cus D’Amato. D’Amato became a major influence on the young fighter, helping him develop the skills and discipline that took him to the top of the sport.In 1986, Tyson became the youngest heavyweight champion in boxing history at 20. His speed, power and aggressive style made him one of the most feared fighters of his era. But success in the ring did not mean that the difficulties in his personal life had disappeared.Tyson later spoke about the challenges he faced while growing up and the personal changes he needed to make. His story is not simply about a young man escaping poverty through sport. It is also about the difference between learning to fight opponents and learning to handle life away from the ring.One of the hardest moments in Tyson’s life came in May 2009, when his daughter Exodus died following an accident involving a treadmill cord at her home in Phoenix, Arizona. She was four years old.Tyson was in Las Vegas when he learned about the accident and travelled to Phoenix. The loss was a personal tragedy that no sporting achievement could ease. In an interview on The Oprah Winfrey Show, reported by the Associated Press on October 12, 2009, Tyson called Exodus “my angel.”He also spoke about his family’s importance to him, saying his children were “the only thing that matters to me now.” CBS NewsThe tragedy also brought Tyson’s struggle with grief into public view. In a 2010 interview with CNN’s Larry King, he described the loss as a moment that forced him to grow up and wake up. When asked whether he would ever get over it, Tyson admitted he did not know.His words showed that grief was not something he could simply put behind him. He had to keep living while finding a way to deal with the loss. The death of Exodus remains an important part of his family story, but it should not be reduced to a simple tale of personal redemption.Tyson’s experience in boxing gave him a clear view of the physical and mental demands of the sport. He knew what it meant to train under pressure, absorb punishment and live with the expectation of winning. He did not want his children to feel they had to follow the same path to make him proud.During an appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience, Tyson discussed the freedom he wanted his children to have. Speaking about the pressure parents can place on young athletes, he explained that he did not want his children to feel they had to become the best at everything.His family includes children with different interests and ambitions. Amir Tyson studied broadcast journalism at American University and later built a career in media and business. Miguel Tyson has explored photography and filmmaking, while Morocco Tyson has shown an interest in sports.Their lives have not followed one shared plan. That is an important part of the story: allowing children to choose their own direction does not mean they must all avoid sports or follow a particular idea of success.Amir Tyson’s education and work in media gave him a route outside his father’s original career. He graduated with a degree in broadcast journalism in 2019 and later launched the clothing brand Debonair. He has also worked in boxing commentary, showing that he can build a career around sport without simply copying his father’s achievements.However, Amir’s story has taken a new turn. In September 2026, he officially signed a multi-fight deal with Misfits Boxing. While his professional debut was initially targeted for December, the bout was postponed to February 2027 following the sudden passing of his trainer. Despite the delay, his decision to enter the ring means the idea that all of Tyson’s sons have stayed away from fighting is no longer accurate.Miguel, meanwhile, has explored creative work, including photography and filmmaking. His interests offer another example of how the children have developed their own identities beyond their father’s fame.For Tyson, fatherhood has also meant living with the consequences of his own choices. His past includes serious personal struggles, and his public story has never been free of controversy. Becoming a parent did not erase those experiences, but it gave him another responsibility: supporting his children as they make decisions for themselves.That is what makes his family life more complicated, and more human, than a simple story about a famous fighter raising gentle sons. His children have their own goals, and their decisions will not always match his wishes.Tyson’s career brought him fame at an age when most people are still finding their place in the world. His childhood, rise to heavyweight champion and later personal struggles have all been documented. Yet his experiences as a father reveal a different part of his life.The death of Exodus showed the limits of fame and physical strength in the face of a personal loss. His comments about his children also show that he values their ability to make their own choices rather than living under the pressure of his reputation.His family life is not a perfect story, and there is no need to present it that way. Amir’s decision to enter boxing shows that Tyson’s children are free to choose paths that may differ from what their father once imagined for them.What matters is the opportunity to make those decisions for themselves. Tyson’s story offers a reminder that a parent’s legacy is not measured only by trophies, titles or money. It can also be seen in the space children are given to build lives of their own.
Article Summary: Mike Tyson’s life has been shaped by boxing victories, personal struggles and the loss of his four-year-old daughter, Exodus, in 2009. The former heavyweight champion has also spoken openly about how fatherhood changed his outlook on life. Tyson did not want his children to feel they had to follow the same path to make him proud.

Article Title: Warriors’ Stephen Curry sends heartwarming 7-word message to Charlotte Hornets legend’s news
Article Text:
Stephen Curry. Image via: Tim Warner/ Getty Images

What did Stephen Curry say about Muggsy Bogues’ jersey retirement?

Why are the Hornets retiring Muggsy Bogues’ No. 1 jersey?

The Charlotte Hornets announced Tuesday that they will retire Muggsy Bogues’ No. 1 jersey, and Stephen Curry sent his congratulations in just seven words. The Warriors superstar grew up in Charlotte while father Dell Curry played for the Hornets, so the news hit close to home. The ceremony is set for halftime of the Hornets’ game against the Milwaukee Bucks on Feb. 11, 2027, at Spectrum Center. Bogues found out while filming what he thought was a Jr. NBA promo, when the script on the screen said otherwise.Stephen Curry wrote, “Yessir there’s only one Muggy Bogues. Congratulations.” He was among the people who reached out after the Hornets shared the reveal video on Instagram.The link goes back decades. Dell Curry played in Charlotte from 1987 to 1998, which put his son in the same locker rooms as Bogues, the Hornets’ primary playmaker in the 1990s. Dell’s No. 30 is already retired there. Bobby Phills’ No. 13 is the other. Bogues will be the third.The reveal was a setup. Bogues sat down to read a teleprompter for what he believed was a Jr. NBA and Jr. WNBA video, and the lines turned out to announce his own night. He got emotional as Dell Curry and Hornets staff told him how much he deserved it. Bogues said he can’t wait to share the night with his family and the fans.Bogues is the shortest player in NBA history at 5-foot-3. The average player during his career stood 6-foot-7 and weighed 213 pounds, which made him 16 inches shorter and 77 pounds lighter.Before the league, he helped Dunbar High School in Baltimore go 60-0 across his junior and senior seasons.Washington drafted him 12th in 1987, and Charlotte took him in the 1988 expansion draft. He stayed through 1998 and is still the franchise leader in assists, steals and minutes. In 632 games with the Hornets, he averaged 8.8 points and 8.8 assists.Over 14 NBA seasons he averaged 7.7 points and 7.6 assists, and only eight players from the 1987 draft class played more games. He was also part of the franchise’s first playoff series win in 1993.Bogues said when the jersey goes up, “it’ll be like I’m the one looking down at the entire world.” Co-chairmen Rick Schnall and Gabe Plotkin called him “a role model for generations.”He has been a Hornets ambassador since 2014.
Article Summary: Muggsy Bogues is the shortest player in NBA history at 5-foot-3. The ceremony is set for halftime of the Hornets’ game against the Milwaukee Bucks on Feb. 11, 2027. Bogues found out while filming what he thought was a Jr. NBA promo.

Article Title: ‘Khelunga bhi waise hi’: Abhishek Sharma reveals Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's ‘Bhaag Milkha Bhaag’ message before NZ blitz

India opener Abhishek Sharma revealed that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi had promised to bat fearlessly, borrowing an iconic dialogue from the Bollywood film, during a net session before the third T20I against New Zealand. The 15-year-old then delivered on his words with an explosive innings that helped India seal the series.Sooryavanshi told Abhishek he would play in the same manner as the character in the film, using the dialogue, “Bhaiya, khelunga bhi waise hi”, which translates to “Brother, I will play the same way”.The young left-hander lived up to his promise, smashing 45 off just 19 balls to give India a flying start in their chase of 199. Opening alongside Sooryavanshi, Abhishek went on to blast 113 off 38 deliveries as India cruised to a six-wicket victory in just 13.2 overs at the Hnry Stadium on Tuesday.Speaking in a video shared by the BCCI after the match, Abhishek recalled the conversation and credited Sooryavanshi's aggressive start with helping set the tone for the chase.“Yesterday, Vaibhav told me something in the nets that I will play the same way as in the Milkha Singh movie Bhag Milkha Bhag dialogue ‘Bhaiya, khelunga bhi waise hi’,” Abhishek said.The India opener explained that Sooryavanshi's intent was particularly significant against New Zealand's frontline fast bowler. Watching from the non-striker's end, Abhishek said the teenager's aggression immediately lifted his confidence.“When you are chasing 200 or 190, his first ball, first over, is his main fast baller. And if you show such aggression as an opener. Because I was on the other side, so I saw that. On the first ball, the non-striker gets excited,” he said.Abhishek was quick to acknowledge the youngster's contribution to the result, stressing that the opening partnership played a crucial role in India's successful chase.“I feel special mention to Vaibhav. What he did today, I think, played a very crucial role today. So it goes to him,” he added.The pair's onslaught rewrote the record books as India raced to 118 without losing a wicket in the powerplay, registering the highest team total in the first six overs of a men's T20 International. India also reached 50 in just 2.2 overs, equalling the joint-fastest team fifty in the format, before crossing the 100-run mark inside five overs.Abhishek also highlighted the selfless attitude within the Indian dressing room, pointing to Sanju Samson 's willingness to adjust his position in the batting order after opening in the first two matches.“One more thing. Sanju Bhai was opening the game. We can see that everyone is selfless. The atmosphere that the team showed today. It must be easy for everyone,” he said.“I feel like Sanju Bhai showed his character. The whole team showed their character,” he added.While the batters dominated the headlines, Abhishek also credited India's bowlers for laying the foundation for the emphatic victory. New Zealand finished with 198/3, with Daryl Mitchell remaining unbeaten on 89 off 52 balls, but India managed to keep the target within reach.Abhishek praised the efforts of Axar Patel , Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav and Nitish Kumar Reddy, whose contributions helped India launch their record-breaking chase."The way the bowlers came back, Akshar Paaji, Bhuvi Paaji, Arsh, Prince, and NK especially, who is a complete all-rounder. Because of that, the total was low today. And we were able to play like this," he said.
Article Summary: India beat New Zealand by six wickets in third T20 International. Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit centuries in emphatic win. Sharma revealed Sooryvanshi had promised to bat fearlessly in the nets. India opener also praised bowlers for laying the foundation for victory.

Article Title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s 25-year bond transcends 30 Grand Slams as tennis icons rewrite the playbook on family healing and raising grounded children
Article Text:
Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s 25-year bond transcends 30 Grand Slams as tennis icons rewrite the playbook on family healing and raising grounded children (Getty Images)

How did Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf understand each other

Why did Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf let their children choose their own paths

How do Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf balance marriage and ambition

How do Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf support children beyond their family

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf have built a family life that goes beyond their success on the tennis court. The couple, who have won 30 Grand Slam singles titles between them, married on October 22, 2001, and have two children, Jaden and Jaz. As Agassi recently shared in an interview with HELLO!, their children have grown up with their own interests, away from the expectation of following their parents into tennis. Their approach to family life offers a glimpse into how two sporting champions balance fame, marriage and parenthood.Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf both reached the top of tennis after starting the sport at a young age. Agassi won eight Grand Slam singles titles, while Graf won 22. They also each won an Olympic singles gold medal, making them the only two players in tennis history to complete a Career Golden Slam.Their careers brought years of competition, public attention and demanding schedules. Agassi has spoken openly about his complicated relationship with tennis in his autobiography, Open. His experiences included intense training under his father, Mike Agassi, and leaving home as a teenager to train at Nick Bollettieri’s tennis academy in Florida.Graf also began playing tennis as a young child and went on to become one of the sport’s most successful players. Her 22 Grand Slam singles titles included four Australian Open titles, six French Open titles, seven Wimbledon titles and five US Open titles.The pair married in Las Vegas in 2001, after both had established themselves as tennis greats. Their son, Jaden, was born four days after their wedding, and their daughter, Jaz, arrived in October 2003.Agassi and Graf have not expected their children to follow them into professional tennis. Their son, Jaden, chose baseball and developed his skills as a pitcher.Jaden attended the University of Southern California, where he played for the USC Trojans baseball team. In February 2025, Major League Baseball reported that he would represent Germany in the World Baseball Classic qualifiers. The decision gave him an opportunity to pursue a sport different from the one that made his parents famous.His choice also reflects the freedom to develop an identity outside his family’s tennis history. Rather than competing on the same courts as his parents, Jaden has worked towards his own goals in baseball.Their daughter, Jaz, has pursued interests that include dance and equestrian activities. Both children have grown up with parents who understand the demands of professional sport, but their careers have taken different directions.Agassi discussed their upbringing in his September 2026 interview with HELLO! during the Laver Cup in London. He explained how their children had learned by watching their parents’ everyday behaviour and seeing how other people treated them.“They see us, they learn from what we do, not from what we say,” Agassi said.He also described their outlook on life in simple terms: “They’re shockingly balanced,” he added proudly. Yahoo SportsAgassi returned to the tennis spotlight in September 2026 as captain of Team World at the Laver Cup in London. The tournament, held at The O2 from September 25 to 27, brought him back into a team environment after his playing career.Speaking to HELLO! during the event, Agassi explained that Graf understands why tennis remains important to him, even after retirement.“She likes seeing me happy, just like I like seeing her happy,” he said.He added that she understands the value he places on the tournament and the opportunity to connect with the sport again.“She knows this is a week in Laver Cup that I value, that I bond with, that I connect to. It’s a lot of work, but she’s never been scared of me in work mode.”Agassi also joked about the need to balance his professional commitments with time away from work.“I always promised her I wouldn’t be too busy or too bored - because I’m kind of dangerous in both! She appreciates my connection to it, so she’ll smile for a week.”His comments offer a glimpse into how the couple support each other’s interests. Both know what it takes to compete at the highest level, which gives them a shared understanding of the demands that come with professional tennis.Agassi and Graf have also supported causes focused on children’s futures, with education and mental health among their areas of work.Agassi established the Andre Agassi Foundation for Education in 1994. One of its major projects was the Andre Agassi College Preparatory Academy, a public charter school that opened in Las Vegas in 2001. The school aimed to provide children in Historic West Las Vegas with a strong education and prepare them for college. Its operations were later transferred to Democracy Prep in 2017.Graf founded Children for Tomorrow in Hamburg, Germany, in 1998. The organisation supports children and young people who have experienced war, persecution and other forms of organised violence.According to the foundation’s official website, it provides medical and psychological care to affected children and supports their healthy development. The organisation is based at the University Medical Centre Hamburg-Eppendorf and works with children who need help dealing with traumatic experiences.The two initiatives focus on different needs, but both work to give children access to support and opportunities. Agassi’s project centres on education, while Graf’s foundation provides care for children affected by violence and displacement.Their work outside tennis adds another part to their public lives. Alongside their sporting records, they have supported efforts to improve children’s access to education and mental health services.After 25 years of marriage, Agassi and Graf continue to share a life shaped by their experiences in professional sport. Their children have followed different interests, and both parents have spoken about the importance of leading by example. Their family life and charitable work show how their interests now extend well beyond their achievements on the tennis court.
Article Summary: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf have built a family life that goes beyond their success on the tennis court. The couple, who have won 30 Grand Slam singles titles between them, married on October 22, 2001, and have two children, Jaden and Jaz. Their approach to family life offers a glimpse into how two sporting champions balance fame, marriage and parenthood.

Article Title: Three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav dies by suicide
Article Text:
Neeraj Yadav (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian para-athletics was left in shock after three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav allegedly died by suicide at a flat on Tuesday night, sources told TOI. The 42-year-old, who competed in the F55 category, suspected to have consumed poison. A postmortem examination was underway at Delhi’s GTB Hospital on Wednesday at the time of filing the report.Paralympic champion Sumit Antil and fellow para-athlete Vipin Kasana were present at the hospital, sources said. The circumstances surrounding Yadav’s death are yet to be established.India’s chief para-athletics coach S Satyanarayana confirmed the development to TOI, saying he had learnt that Yadav had died by suicide.“Yes, Neeraj has died by suicide. That is what I have also come to know. I have been told that he consumed poison at his flat last night. This is extremely unfortunate and tragic,” Satyanarayana said.The coach suggested that Yadav may have been under emotional distress after missing the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games because of his doping suspension. However, the circumstances that led to his death remain unconfirmed.“He would have been looking forward to competing at these Games. Medals at the Asian Para Games can bring substantial government cash awards and opportunities for stable employment. But his suspension had not ended, and he could not compete. It is possible that this affected him deeply, but we cannot say for certain what he was going through,” Satyanarayana added.Yadav, who hails from Uttar Pradesh, was among India’s accomplished para-athletes. Diagnosed with post-polio residual paralysis at the age of seven, he nevertheless pursued his sporting ambitions. He played wheelchair tennis between 2005 and 2012 before switching to para-athletics.His breakthrough came at the 2015 Delhi State Athletics Meet, where he won gold medals in the shot put, javelin and discus events.Yadav announced himself on the international stage at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, winning gold in the men’s F55 javelin throw with an Asian-record effort of 29.84 metres.He subsequently clinched two gold medals at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games in 2023, winning the javelin and discus events to take his career tally to three Asian Para Games titles.However, his career was clouded by an anti-doping case. The National Anti-Doping Agency provisionally suspended him after an out-of-competition sample collected in Bengaluru in October 2023 tested positive for stanozolol, an anabolic steroid. He later sought DNA testing of his sample through the anti-doping disciplinary process.His death marks a tragic turn in the life of an athlete who overcame significant physical challenges to reach the top of Asian para-athletics.
Article Summary: Three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav allegedly died by suicide. The 42-year-old, who competed in the F55 category, suspected to have consumed poison. A postmortem examination was underway at Delhi’s GTB Hospital on Wednesday.

Article Text:

LUCKNOW: Chief minister Yogi Adityanath praised the youth of the state for turning opportunities and talent into achievements.Before attending the ‘TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards 2026’ in Lucknow on Tuesday, the CM took to social media to talk about the changed work culture in UP under BJP’s double-engine govt since 2017.“Whether it is a new way of thinking in innovation, the courage of entrepreneurship, or the resolve to set new benchmarks of excellence in various fields, the youth power of UP is turning possibilities into achievements through its talent and hard work,” he said.Yogi added that before 2017, UP’s youth had to migrate for lack of opportunities. The state was riddled with corruption, nepotism and disorder, and it was impossible to get jobs on merit. The youth was staring at a bleak future, with no opportunities and encouragement.“After 2017, the double-engine govt changed this work culture. It has created new opportunities for youth by promoting transparent recruitment, skill development, start-ups and entrepreneurship. Today, the youth power of UP is not merely aspiring for jobs but is also forging a new identity in creating employment, playing a leading role in realising the resolve of a ‘Viksit Uttar Pradesh-Viksit Bharat’,” the CM wrote.
