Article Title: 2 million followers, just 33 votes: Poor poll result shocks Jodhpur astro-influencer
Article Text:
Omprakash Bishnoi, a popular astrologer and influencer, contested the sarpanch election in Jodhpur's Indon Ki Dhani-II.





JODHPUR: A huge following on social media does not guarantee a good showing in election results, even if one claims to be able to glance into the future. That is the bitter truth borne out by the sarpanch election at Indon Ki Dhani-II gram panchayat in Osian tehsil of Jodhpur district.This is where astrologer-influencer and YouTuber Omprakash Bishnoi, brimming with confidence in the more than two million followers he commanded across digital platforms, decided to enter the fray for village headman.With more than 1.4 million followers on Instagram and 232,000 on Facebook, besides 550,000 YouTube subscribers, Bishnoi's electoral resume also boasted of the fact that he was president of a local cow shelter.That aside, he was buoyed up by the fact that he was contesting the elections in his native gram panchayat and confident that it would ensure at least some traction among local voters.Or so he thought!In the end, the fortune-telling influencer managed to garner just 33 votes in a village with around 1,600 eligible voters. The electoral rout came as a surprise not just to his legions of online followers but also, presumably, to him.Predictably, the result triggered a buzz online, with many pointing out the irony that a man who claimed to be able to read faces and predict fortunes lacked the ability to predict his own electoral debacle.Following the announcement of the results, Omprakash Bishnoi took to his official social media accounts to thank voters of his native village and accept their verdict gracefully.Referring to the Hindi saying, “There is darkness beneath the lamp”, he acknowledged the irony of failing to win support in his own village despite his popularity online.His dignified response to defeat, while drawing appreciation on social media, raises a pertinent question: can millions of online followers ever be a substitute for the trust of grassroots voters? In Bishnoi’s own, albeit unexpected experience, they surely cannot!
Article Summary: Omprakash Bishnoi, a popular astrologer and influencer, contested the sarpanch election in Jodhpur's Indon Ki Dhani-II gram panchayat. The electoral rout came as a surprise not just to his legions of online followers but also, presumably, to him.

Article Title: Amazon updates AI usage rules for engineers, sends memo: We are seeing the beginning of AI’s effect on software engineering
Article Text:
Read full memo Amazon sent to engineers

Amazon engineering leaders have updated the role guidelines for Software Development Engineers (SDEs) to reflect that real-world results matter a lot more than specific tools. A company memo by Terk Terkowitz, vice president and distinguished engineer at Worldwide Amazon Stores, outlined leadership’s vision to move towards “Renaissance Developers” that combine human judgement and artificial intelligence, or AI. They urged engineers to integrate AI into their daily routines or risk being left behind, noting that AI will sit at the center of future engineering practices.Amazon cautioned against evaluating performance solely on “flawed” input metrics, such as the amount of tokens or lines of code, which could increase costs and complexity. Rather, leaders should look to the longer-term impacts on customers and businesses. Engineers were reminded that learning where AI falls short is “a finding, not a failing.” The memo also urged managers and individual contributors to keep their hands on AI tools but stay deeply connected to customer needs, ensuring tech adoption translates into tangible business results.An update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AIAmazon engineering leaders revised the role guideline for software development engineers, underscoring what matters most is the outcome, not which tools are used.Written by Terk Terkowitz, VP/Distinguished Engineer, Worldwide Amazon StoresOne of the biggest shifts our leadership teams are seeing right now is how AI is changing the way software development engineers (SDEs) do their work, while balancing that the important elements of being an SDE are the same.Engineering leadership, including Distinguished and Senior Principal Engineers, from across Amazon recently came together to reaffirm what it means to be an SDE at Amazon. Based on key learnings and observations from the most successful SDEs at the company, they developed an updated role guideline. Our most prolific engineers have demonstrated that neither the developer role nor their output is defined by the use of AI. We're now in the era of the Renaissance Developer, blending AI tools with human judgment and domain expertise to build entirely new things. As a leader in agentic AI with thousands of SDEs, Amazon believes sharing our vision for the SDE role of the future can serve as a model for our customers.The following is a memo shared with software engineers across Amazon.-TerkDear SDEs and SDMs,As we developed the new version of the role guideline for Software Development Engineers (SDEs) at Amazon, we faced an important question: how much do we focus on AI? Historically we have tried to avoid having the SDE role guidelines be explicit about technology, reflecting the diversity of businesses that Amazon is in, and the work that our SDEs do. We have held to that approach as two decades of technology trends (the cloud, microservices, serverless, etc. ) have reshaped the work that SDEs do. In the Senior Principal and Distinguished Engineer communities, we have deeply debated whether this time is different. AI is changing the work of software engineering both more quickly and more fundamentally than these previous trends. What it means to be a software engineer, and what software engineering even is, is changing quickly and durably.Despite the speed of change, we believe that it is still early. We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind. We’re just seeing the beginning of AI’s effect on software engineering. While we have a vision for what the future looks like, there’s a lot that’s still emerging. We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice. If you haven’t already, you should take the time to learn and apply AI into your daily work as soon as possible. If you’re already using AI, keep investing in finding better practice, and keep learning. The pace of change is high.It is difficult to define, in a way that will stand the test of time, what good AI powered engineering practices look like. Any definition we write now will likely look antiquated by this time next year. Antiquated definitions run the risk of slowing our progress, freezing our engineering practices in amber while the world moves on without us. To solve this problem, we have decided to focus on what is not changing as we evolved the SDE roles. Specifically, impact on our customers, our businesses, and our teams. The outcomes that matter aren’t changing, even if the inputs, tools, and techniques are changing faster than ever.“What’s going to change in the next five to ten years?” But I very rarely get asked “What’s not going to change in the next five to ten years?” That second question is actually the more important of the two.Jeff Bezos2012 interview with Werner VogelsThis conclusion made it easier to write the role guideline, but likely leaves you, our SDEs and SDMs, with an important question about how you should be using AI, and how you should be measuring AI usage in your teams and organizations. We believe that it is best to measure, and be measured by, long-term outcomes. But these outcomes can be time delayed, difficult to measure, and hard to isolate from other trends. In some cases, we have tackled those problems by using input metrics instead, like token usage or adoption of AI tools, or throughput metrics like code changes and reviews. We are all aware of how deeply flawed these metrics are, primarily because they are disconnected from what matters. We know that using these metrics could, if used as a target instead of a measure, drive negative outcomes, increasing costs (tokenmaxxing is at odds with frugality), and increasing complexity (measuring LOC is at odds with invent and simplify). We believe that this community, with your strong ownership and focus on delivering results, will help us avoid these negative outcomes.More positively, we have found that these input metrics correlate well with the outputs that matter and expect they will continue to do so for some time. This effect is driven both by increasing productivity and delivery on teams that have embraced AI the most (we call them frontier teams), and that teams and individuals who are not adopting AI or increasing output metrics are falling behind. Using these input metrics, with care and judgement, as you think about your career and your organization’s performance is appropriate. We recommend paying special attention to the 10th percentile (finding those teams who aren’t embracing AI effectively and understanding why) and the 90th percentile (finding those teams who are heavily using AI and understanding whether they’re seeing delivery increases to match) of AI adoption. Working together, over time, we will find better metrics and set smarter goals.“Good inventors and designers deeply understand their customer. They spend tremendous energy developing that intuition. They study and understand many anecdotes rather than only the averages you’ll find on surveys.”Jeff Bezos2016 Letter to ShareholdersTo paraphrase: Good leaders deeply understand their team's work. They spend tremendous energy developing that intuition. They study and understand many anecdotes, and carefully track outputs, rather than only surface-level metrics.If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing. Document why, share it with your community of peers, bring it to your manager, and work to find solutions. An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for.As a technical or organizational leader, part of your job is making sure that your team or organization is using AI to the best effect to improve delivery for customers and your business. That requires deeply understanding these technologies yourself, working with them hands-on rather than relying on what you hear, and understanding how others are using them. Sufficient understanding means you have used these tools on your production work, can describe a task where they helped and a task where they did not, and can explain that judgement to your team. Deploying AI in your organizations requires carefully balancing between exploring new and better ways to do things and investing in doubling down on the ones you already have. Judgement and care are key. As a leader, we expect you to be taking ownership of connecting the inputs and outputs in your team or organization.As we have looked across our organizations, we have found that the leaders who are having the most impact are those doubling down on learn and be curious. Both spending the time they need to learn AI and making time for the people they lead to do the same. We have seen that the returns on this investment in our organizations are disproportionately large, with teams who have followed their curiosity (appropriately balanced with deliver results and insist on the highest standards) seeing the most positive impact from AI adoption.We have also found that SDEs and SDMs who are closer to their products and businesses are able to take the most advantage of AI and agentic software development. As Amazon has grown, we’ve seen some of our ICs and SDMs become less connected to their customers and business. We want to reverse this trend. We recommend that ICs of all levels find ways to become deeply connected to your customers, and your team or org’s product direction. As always, the scope and depth of this ownership will increase as you become more senior. For SDMs, we also recommend spending time making sure you’re close to your customers and business, and you’re helping the ICs in your organization to do the same.This is a time of change for our industry, and a time of change for what it means to be a software engineer. We believe that the opportunity for software, and for software engineers, has never been larger. We’re more excited about the future of software development, and of our role as engineers, than ever before. Partnering with you as strong, curious, customer-obsessed owners, we will invent the future of software development together.We will continue to evolve the SDE role over the coming years, as AI’s effect on our business and engineering practices becomes clear. But we believe that’s unlikely to change what really matters: obsession with our customers, and a long-term focus on delivering results.
Article Summary: Amazon engineering leaders have updated the role guidelines for Software Development Engineers (SDEs) They urge engineers to integrate AI into their daily routines or risk being left behind. Amazon cautioned against evaluating performance solely on “flawed” input metrics.

Article Title: Class 12 student found hanging at her home in Delhi, family suspects foul play
Article Text:
(AI image) A 17-year-old Class 12 student was found hanging from a ceiling fan at her home in Wazirpur JJ Colony





NEW DELHI: A 17-year-old Class 12 student was found hanging from a ceiling fan at her home in northwest Delhi’s Wazirpur JJ Colony on Tuesday, police said.The girl, identified as Muskan, was a student at a Sarvodaya Vidyalaya.According to police, the incident came to light when her family members were away.Following a PCR call, the girl was taken to DCB Hospital, where doctors declared her brought dead.Her mother told police that Muskan was found hanging inside the house. The family has suspected foul play, and police are investigating the matter.No suicide note was found at the spot, police said. The body has been sent to Babu Jagjivan Ram Memorial (BJRM) Hospital for a postmortem examination.Police have initiated an inquiry and are investigating all possible angles.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: A 17-year-old Class 12 student was found hanging from a ceiling fan at her home in northwest Delhi’s Wazirpur JJ Colony on Tuesday. The girl, identified as Muskan, was a student at a Sarvodaya Vidyalaya.

Article Title: “I’m getting to play with these kids": Lewis Hamilton opens up about Kim Kardashian’s kids as speculation about a baby grows
Article Text:
Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton (Getty Images)

Lewis Hamilton reveals his bond with Kim Kardashian’s children

Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton face renewed baby speculation

Us Weekly

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lewis Hamilton has offered a rare glimpse into his relationship with Kim Kardashian’s children, revealing a thoughtful gesture that has brought him closer to her family. The Formula 1 champion shared that he bought a dog named Halo for Kim’s four children, North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm. His warm comments came as speculation continues about whether the couple could welcome a child together. While neither has confirmed plans to expand their family, Hamilton’s remarks have drawn fresh attention to the bond he is building with the children.Hamilton opened up about family life while speaking to reporters during an event at the United States Grand Prix in Texas. Asked what brings him happiness away from racing, the seven-time world champion spoke affectionately about his niece and nephew before mentioning Kim’s children.“My niece and nephew always bring me a lot of happiness [and so do] my girlfriend’s kids. I love spending time with them. She’s got four.”He then revealed that he had surprised the children with a pet, giving fans a glimpse of a more personal side of his relationship with the reality star.“I’m getting to play with these kids, and I got them a dog this year. So, little Halo is a new member of that family,” he said.Halo, a golden retriever puppy, has already appeared on Kim’s social media.The gift suggests Hamilton has found a place in the family’s everyday life, although the couple has kept most details of their relationship private.Kim shares four children with her former husband, Kanye West. North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm have occasionally appeared in social media posts featuring Hamilton. The pair knew each other for years before their romance became public, which may have helped make their time together feel more familiar.Hamilton’s comments have also revived interest in reports that the couple may want a child together. An August report from, citing an unnamed source, claimed Kim had considered having more children with the British racing driver.“They are really in love. Kim may want to have more kids with Lewis,” the source said. “They just get each other, they get each other’s quirks. She is really happy with him.”The source also described the couple as well matched, saying their shared drive and understanding had helped their relationship.However, the reports remain unconfirmed. Neither Kim nor Hamilton has publicly announced plans to have a baby together, and his latest comments focused on the happiness he finds in spending time with the children she already has.For now, the clearest takeaway is Hamilton’s growing connection with Kim’s family. Whether that bond eventually leads to a bigger family remains an open question, not a confirmed plan.
Article Summary: Lewis Hamilton reveals his bond with Kim Kardashian's children. Formula 1 champion bought a dog named Halo for Kim's four children, North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm. Comments come as speculation continues about whether the couple could welcome a child together.

Article Title: Tribals protest demolition drive on Kharghar hill after man found dead
Article Text:
The protesting tribals blamed the Cidco officials for the man's death





Navi Mumbai: A demolition drive by Cidco’s CUC (Controller of Unauthorised Construction) team to raze encroachments by illegal shanties and a canteen shed at the tribal hamlet on Kharghar hill at Belpada on Tuesday morning was protested by the tribals after a physically challenged tribal man was found dead in a shanty. The local tribals alleged that Cidco officials were responsible for his death by carrying out the demolition without checking whether the shanty was occupied or not.Following the incident, Cidco said in a press release that, during the eviction drive, it razed an unauthorised commercial structure consisting of a brick building and a tarpaulin-sheet shed. It said that the allegations that a tribal man died during the drive are false, as no action was taken on the hutment where the tribal man was found dead. Therefore, the question of his death during the eviction campaign does not arise. On the contrary, when the hutment of the concerned tribal man was inspected from outside by the CUC team, it was found that the man was already lying injured inside the hutment; hence, an ambulance was called, and he was taken to Panvel sub-district hospital, where he was declared brought dead.The local tribals accompanying the deceased man’s kin gathered at Kharghar police station and demanded that an FIR should be registered against the Cidco officials concerned, alleging that they were responsible for the physically challenged tribal man’s death while carrying out the demolition drive by razing down the hutment.Tribals argued with the Cidco officials and the local police after a Cidco official in the CUC team claimed that the man’s body was deliberately kept inside the hutment before the demolition drive to blame Cidco for his death while carrying out the demolition. The argument was recorded by the locals, and it went viral on social media.Suresh Mengade, Cidco’s chief vigilance officer, said, “The CUC team had gone to the Adivasi hamlet atop Kharghar hill for demolition of an illegal canteen being constructed using a tarpaulin shed and bricks, as despite serving two notices to evacuate the encroachment on Cidco land, the concerned person constructing the illegal canteen did not evacuate. After razing down the illegal canteen, the CUC team, while coming down the hill, spotted five shanties encroaching on Cidco land. Hence, the CUC team, along with local police, razed down one shanty after confirming that only wood logs were stored inside. When the team checked the adjacent hutment, a physically challenged man, with an amputated right hand below the elbow, was lying motionless. He had a head injury with dried blood which indicated it might be two days old injury and also injury to his hand and blood accumulated in eyes. Hence, the police took him in an ambulance to Panvel sub-district hospital. The post-mortem report will reveal the date and time of the tribal man’s death.”Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar, said, “Prima facie, we have registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) which will be followed by an in-depth probe.”
Article Summary: A demolition drive by Cidco’s CUC ( Controller of Unauthorised Construction) team to raze encroachments by illegal shanties and a canteen shed at the tribal hamlet on Kharghar hill at Belpada on Tuesday morning was protested by the tribals. A physically challenged tribal man was found dead in a shanty. The local tribals alleged that Cid co officials were responsible for his death.

Article Title: 3 lives snuffed out due to Central Railway disruptions in Mumbai, allege kin; demand compensation
Article Text:
Two men, Rahul Rajbhar and Kharbhan Rajbhar, died after being hit by a train during railway disruptions.





MUMBAI: Two men, distant-relatives-turned-friends, died after being hit by a train on the tracks between Ghatkopar and Vikhroli stations on Monday amid disruptions on Central Railway.Now, their relatives are left scouring paperwork and looking for any video evidence to challenge the official claim that the duo was illegally crossing railway tracks. Relatives said a stalled train might have caused Rahul Rajbhar (22) and Kharbhan Rajbhar (35) to alight and their kin should be compensated by the Railways.CR suburban services faced major disruption on Monday after a fire in the relay room near Kanjurmarg brought the signalling system to a halt. The disruption lasted around nine hours, with services continuing to run 30-40 minutes late until late in the evening even after operations were restored across the affected routes. Thousands of commuters were stranded in stationary trains for 70-90 minutes, while some walked along the tracks as services operated intermittently on adjoining lines.Although services were largely on time during Tuesday morning’s peak hours, some trains in the afternoon were delayed by 15-20 minutes, causing further inconvenience to commuters.CR is expected to conclude its inquiry into the cause of the Kanjurmarg fire on Wednesday.Rahul and Kharbhan came to the city from Uttar Pradesh about three years ago. Just like a dozen other family members, the two worked as stack parking welders.According to the police, both men appear to have boarded a train from the eastern suburbs after finishing work and were headed home to Thane. “There is a possibility that due to the CR disruptions, the two alighted from the train and were to exit the railway premises to travel home by road,” said a police officer. Around 7.55 pm, a Kalyan - CSMT local hit them between Ghatkopar and Vikhroli stations. “We will be recording the motorman’s statement and looking for witnesses,” the officer said.None of their relatives knew where Rahul and Kharbhan had boarded the train from on Monday or what exactly transpired. “Railway officials said the two were crossing the tracks. But because the train had halted for a long time, they must have decided to alight or it is possible that they fell off a train. The cause needs to be investigated,” said Prakash Rajbhar, a relative. He said the family is trying to collect all the paperwork related to the incident so that a claim for compensation can be filed.Another relative, Aniket Rajbhar, said Kharbhan leaves behind his widow and four children at their hometown. “We need to know what happened; at least show us the CCTV footage or relevant reports. Police just said a motorman alerted them about the bodies,” he said.Rahul’s distant aunt, who spoke to TOI at Rajawadi Hospital postmortem centre in Ghatkopar while waiting to collect the body, said the last time she had met him was when he was seven. Rahul was single.The relatives claimed their bodies on Tuesday evening and left for their hometown in a hearse. They will be covering a distance of over 1,600 km in 30 hours.In a separate incident, a college-goer, Sahil Thete (21), had died after being hit by a train at Bhandup station on Monday. His family alleged that the accident was a result of railway disruptions. “Sahil studied in the last year of B.Com. His parents sell flowers garlands and he would assist them. On Monday, he went to his coaching class at Thane. Typically, he would take a train to reach his Kanjurmarg residence after class. But on Monday, the railway timetable was a mess. Sahil could only alight at Bhandup. He was probably trying to exit the railway station when he was killed,” said Sagar, a neighbour.Police said Sahil was crossing from platform no. 4 to platform no. 2 on the tracks when a fast train hit him on platform no. 3 of Bhandup. “Sahil had a bright future ahead of him, but the railway disruption snuffed out his life. The Railways must offer one of his sisters a job so they can look after their parents,” said Sagar.The Kurla Government Railway Police have recorded separate cases of accidental deaths and are probing the sequence of events leading to the three fatalities.
Article Summary: Two men, distant-relatives-turned-friends, died after being hit by a train on the tracks on Monday amid disruptions on Central Railway. Relatives are left scouring paperwork and looking for any video evidence to challenge the official claim that the duo was illegally crossing railway tracks. Thousands of commuters were stranded in stationary trains for 70-90 minutes.

Article Title: Central Railway mulls opening staff-only special local to Mumbai commuters after viral video of locked coaches during train disruption draws criticism
Article Text:
File pic for representation

Mumbai:

CR inquiry into Kanjurmarg relay room fire likely to conclude on Wednesday





Central Railway is considering opening a staff-only special local to regular commuters on part of its route or cancelling the service altogether after railway employees allegedly kept its coach doors locked during Monday’s suburban train disruption following a fire at Kanjurmarg.A decision on the action to be taken is expected after a meeting of senior railway officials.The incident occurred on a special fast local from CSMT to Kalyan , which departs at 4.30pm daily and is reserved for railway employees. The train halts at Byculla, Parel, Matunga, Kurla, Ghatkopar, Thane and Dombivli.Amid the disruption on Monday, the coach doors were allegedly locked from inside after the train crossed Kurla. When the train reached Thane, commuters waiting on the platform tried to board but were unable to enter the coach as the doors remained shut. A video showing the incident went viral, drawing criticism as crowded platforms and a shortage of trains left commuters struggling to reach home.The incident triggered criticism on social media, with commuters questioning the operation of staff-only services during a major disruption and demanding that they be opened to the public.Sameer Mohite, posting on X, appealed to Central Railway, the Mumbai divisional railway manager and Railway Ministry to convert workmen special services into regular services.“Just look at all the railway staffs laughing and enjoying the sufferings on Taxpayer commuters,” he wrote.Another user, posting under the handle Gandharva, questioned the decision to operate the service during the crisis. “Why did @Central_Railway operate a workmen special in an ongoing crisis where commute by a regular local train was a struggle itself?” the post said.Himanshu Mukherjee also criticised the railway administration, alleging that commuters were struggling to travel while railway staff on the special local refused to let passengers board. He wrote that Mumbaikars were being crushed in crowded trains, hanging from train gates and waiting for hours at stations, while the workmen special continued to operate.Central Railway has taken note of the incident and is considering two options. One is to cancel the staff-only special local permanently. The other is to run it as a fast service exclusively for railway employees between CSMT and Matunga, and then operate it on the slow line from Matunga to Kalyan, allowing regular commuters to board it on the latter stretch.Senior officials will decide which course of action to adopt, railway authorities said.Central Railway is expected to conclude its inquiry into the cause of the fire at the signalling relay room at Kanjurmarg on Wednesday.The fire, reported at 9.33am on Monday, left around 24 signals across all six lines between Vikhroli and Bhandup blank, severely disrupting suburban services for nearly nine hours. Railway officials suspect excessive heat or an electrical fault may have triggered the blaze, but the exact cause is yet to be established. The signalling system was restored in stages, with all affected lines operational by 7.35pm. However, services continued to run 30-40 minutes late until late in the evening.Although services were largely on time during Tuesday morning’s peak hours, some trains in the afternoon were delayed by 15-20 minutes, causing further inconvenience to commuters.
Article Summary: CR inquiry into Kanjurmarg relay room fire likely to conclude on Wednesday. Incident occurred on a special fast local from CSMT to Kalyan, which departs at 4.30pm daily. Train halts at Byculla, Parel, Matunga, Kurla, Ghatkopar, Thane and Dombivli.

Article Title: 7 lakh elderly learners write test under ULLAS in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Elderly woman who appeared for the Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Assessment Test Dhoregaon cluster in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Sunday

Mangal Baban Mane, in yellow sari, writes the exam in one of the exam centres in Kolhapur

One of the exam centres in Kolhapur





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR/KOLHAPUR/NASHIK: A grandson taught his grandmother her first letters. Another proudly accompanied his grandfather to an exam. On Sunday, together, they turned a literacy test into a celebration of second chances.Sixty-five-year-old Mangal Baban Mane of Kolhapur once dreamt of becoming a govt officer. Life had other plans. Poverty and circumstances cut short her education. On Sunday, decades later, she took her seat for Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Assessment Test (FLNAT), carrying with her lessons taught not by a teacher, but by her grandson.“My grandson is in Class V. He taught me Marathi letters and helped me learn words. He also taught me counting from one to 100,” Mane said. “Now I can do basic addition and subtraction. Most importantly, I can write my own name.”Hundreds of kilometres away in Nashik, science graduate Shashank Borse proudly escorted his 68-year-old grandfather to another examination centre.The older man had spent his life in the fields so that future generations could study. On Sunday, it was his turn to become the student.Together, their stories captured the spirit of a remarkable statewide exercise that saw nearly seven lakh elderly learners appear for FLNAT under the ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society) programme of New India Literacy Programme (NILP).For Vimal Kanu, 60, from Satara’s Man taluka, the examination marked another milestone in a journey of self-belief. She had appeared last year but did not clear the test. This time, she walked into the classroom with confidence.“The change in my life is visible,” she said. “Earlier, I used a thumb impression. Now I sign my name. I can read small words and understand what is written. I can even check whether a shopkeeper has returned the correct balance,” she added.Across Maharashtra , elderly men and women who had missed out on schooling decades ago returned to classrooms, many writing their first formal examination. The test, conducted in nine languages, including Marathi, Hindi, English and Urdu, is part of govt’s effort to bring non-literate adults into the education system.“Around seven lakh learners registered on the ULLAS app appeared for the examination. Those who qualify can continue their education through standards three, five, eight, 10 and 12 equivalents,” said education director (planning) Krishnakumar Patil.“He spent his youth working on the farm so the generations after him could study,” Borse said of his grandfather. “Because of his sacrifices, my father became a teacher and I found a job in Nashik. Taking him to this exam was one of the proudest moments of our lives. He is the only one among seven siblings who dared to take the test. I hope others now follow him,” Borse said.The response was especially strong in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, where more than 41,000 candidates appeared at 2,698 centres. Against a target of 47,368 learners, 43,700 had registered for the programme.Officials said the initiative extends beyond literacy.“Through FLNAT, we aim to build financial, legal and digital literacy, along with health awareness and other life skills that help improve quality of life,” Patil said.The scale of the literacy drive came alive at the Dhoregaon cluster, where 198 neo-literates turned up to write the test at Zilla Parishad Central Primary School and its satellite centres. Guided by centre head Sachin Damale, in-charge headmaster Rajesh Hiwale and a team of teachers, the centres transformed into classrooms of second chances as elderly learners, many writing an examination for the first time in their lives, took their seats with quiet determination. “They were welcomed with flowers before the exam,” said Hiwale. “The welcome eased their fears and boosted their confidence. The most memorable sight was seeing elderly learners arrive with their grandchildren, who watched with pride as their grandparents read, wrote and solved questions on their own.”The examination carried 150 marks and required a minimum score of 33%.For many candidates, however, the day’s biggest achievement was not the result that will arrive later. It was simply walking into a classroom, taking a seat and writing the test.
Article Summary: Elderly men and women who had missed out on schooling decades ago returned to classrooms, many writing their first formal examination. The test, conducted in nine languages, including Marathi, Hindi, English and Urdu, is part of govt's effort to bring non-literate adults into the education system.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Bengaluru artistes bring ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ to life at Dombivli Navratri festival
Article Text:
Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.





DOMBIVLI: A theatrical portrayal of Goddess Durga’s battle against demon Mahishasura offered Dombivli residents a glimpse into India’s traditional performing arts during the Sharadiya Navratri festival.Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale of the goddess’s victory to life.The programme was organised as part of the Navratri celebrations hosted by the Dr Shrikant Shinde Foundation and Shri Navdurga Yuva Mandal at the DNC school grounds in Dombivli East.Kalyan MP Dr Shrikant Shinde, who attended the event, stressed the importance of preserving and promoting traditional art forms that reflect India's cultural heritage.“Artistic performances that preserve our culture and traditions are important. They need encouragement and support so that this rich heritage can be passed on to future generations,” Shinde said.The presentation centred on the story of Mahishasura, whose tyranny threatened the world until Goddess Durga took the form of Mahishasuramardini to defeat him.Through a combination of theatrical expression, dance and devotional elements, the Bengaluru artistes depicted the goddess’s strength and the victory of righteousness over evil.Organisers said the festival seeks to go beyond religious rituals by providing a platform for India's diverse cultural and spiritual traditions. Alongside devotional activities, the programme features performances showcasing different forms of traditional art.At a time when modern entertainment platforms are increasingly popular, such performances offer an opportunity to introduce younger audiences to India's mythological stories and traditional artistic expressions.They also help preserve cultural practices that have been passed down through generations.The Navratri festival has included a range of religious and cultural programmes, including the Navkundatmak Sahasrachandi Mahayag, Haripath, bhajan sessions and devotional music.The organisers have sought to combine religious observances with cultural activities to give visitors a wider experience of the festival.The ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ presentation added a distinctive dimension to this year's celebrations, highlighting the role of traditional theatre in keeping India's mythological narratives and performing arts alive.
Article Summary: Bengaluru artistes presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil. The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale to life.

Article Title: Pune RTO launches WhatsApp number for passengers against fleecing by private bus operators
Article Text:
Photo for representation

Pune:





Diwali travellers who feel that they are being fleeced by private bus operators can complain to the RTO at 8275330209 via WhatsApp, officials said.Officials said that they recently had a meeting with the private bus operators and had asked them to go by the set formula and not to fleece or overcharge passengers. “We have asked them to make sure that they stick to the regulations. As per the formula, the bus operators can increase the fares during the festive season by 50% of the fare of an MSRTC bus of the same make and going to the same destination. They should not deviate from the same. Any passenger who thinks that they have been fleeced can WhatsApp their complaint to us with all details, including the ticket copy, and an investigation will be conducted,” an RTO official said.
Article Summary: Diwali travellers who feel that they are being fleeced by private bus operators can complain to the RTO at 8275330209 via WhatsApp, officials said. As per the formula, the operators can increase the fares during the festive season by 50% of the fare of an MSRTC bus of the same make.

Article Title: Row over Khalid's book: ABVP protests outside IISER Pune, students criticise institute's withdrawal
Article Text:
Pune:





Thirteen students affiliated to ABVP on Tuesday staged a protest in front of the main gate of Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Pune against the decision to include the book based on jailed activist and former JNU researcher Umar Khalid’s PhD thesis in its library.Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Pune had withdrawn the book, ‘Fractured Communities: Adivasi Histories and the Politics of Power’, after its inclusion in the Srinivasa Ramanujan Library triggered a social media controversy over the weekend.Some students of IISER, speaking on condition of anonymity, criticised the institute’s decision, saying it “should have defended the book on its merits. One of them said, “It was a failure on the institute’s part to withdraw a well-researched academic book on the basis of anonymous tweets, without doing due diligence, which should be the foundation of a science institute”.Released earlier this year, ‘Fractured Communities: Adivasi Histories and the Politics of Power’ examines the history of tribal societies Singhbhum (Jharkhand) and is based on Khalid’s PhD thesis at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).Khalid has been lodged in Delhi’s Tihar Jail since 2020 as an undertrial prisoner in connection with a case registered under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and other provisions of law. He was recently named the Asia-Pacific recipient of the Front Line Defenders Award for Human Rights Defenders at Risk.The institute had said the book was retracted “as a precaution in order to avoid any misunderstanding or unrest” after the matter was brought to the authorities’ attention. The controversy began after a photograph of the book displayed on the library’s digital board under the title ‘New Additions of Books’ was shared on ‘X’ by the handle @GemsofAcademia on Saturday night. The post was widely shared, with Madabhushi Madan Gopal, chairperson of the institute’s board of governors, responding through his personal ‘X’ account.“As in-charge chairperson, BoG, IISER Pune, I am shocked to know this. This is retracted last night and action is initiated on those who played this mischief. I assure such things will not happen again in IISER Pune. Prof. Sunil Bhagwat, Director, has taken immediate steps. We need to be alert,” he had written.“Banning of a research thesis-based book is wrong. Since there is nothing anti-national about the lives of Adivasis, why should IISER students not read about it as a part of their broader education? By bowing down to anonymous people on the internet, IISER Pune is setting a dangerous precedent. Science is based on reasoning, which means scientific institutes should defend the critical thinking in students. Why ban a book? Let students read and decide whether they like it or not,” an IISER student said.Another student questioned how a university of such high repute as IISER could introduce or ban anything based on social media trends. “When the book is not banned in India by govt, and is readily available in the open market, why should it be removed from a library?” she said.ABVP, however, questioned the relevance of adding a book authored by a person booked under UAPA. Radhey Bahegavankar, ABVP Pune city secretary, said the organisation’s main demands were an impartial investigation into the decision-making process of the IISER library committee, identification of those who approved the book and action against them.“We submitted our demands to IISER director Sunil Bhagwat. We want action against whoever is responsible for suggesting and approving the book,” said Bahegavankar.
Article Summary: Thirteen students affiliated to ABVP staged a protest in front of the main gate of Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Pune. The decision to include the book based on jailed activist and former JNU researcher Umar Khalid’s PhD thesis in its library triggered a social media controversy. ‘Fractured Communities: Adivasi Histories and the Politics of Power’ examines the history of tribal societies.

Article Title: Man tries to steal cash from ATM unit
Article Text:
Pune:

TOI





A man trying to break into an ATM of a public-sector bank in Sadashiv Peth around 2.15 am on Monday was thwarted by a police constable and detained. He was later released by the police.Senior inspector Navnath Jagtap of Vishrambaug police station told, “The suspect was breaking the ATM unit and the passbook printer in the kiosk when our team spotted him. Before our team could detain him, he had damaged the ATM unit and the passbook printer machine”.“He just wanted to pull out some currency notes, but he failed to do so. Later, we also realised that he has some medical issues and thus, he was released. We have served him a notice asking him to cooperate with the investigation,” police said.
